title: Agent Host: bring back granular "sticky" terminal auto-approve controls (allow for session / always allow exact command line)
body:
Building on the recent work to have [INLINE_CODE] and [INLINE_CODE] respected for Agent Host Copilot (#322633, #322774), I'd like to bring back the more granular, "sticky" approval controls we used to have so users aren't re-prompted for commands they've already OK'd.

Issue:

Today the AH terminal auto-approver ([INLINE_CODE]) only compiles the forwarded [INLINE_CODE] rules and checks each command against them. Unlike the workbench auto-approver ([INLINE_CODE], which has [INLINE_CODE] and shows "Auto approved for this session"), the AH side has **no concept of session-scoped approvals**. So once I approve something, there's no way to make it stick for the rest of the session, and I keep getting re-prompted.

This shows up a lot because terminal auto-approve is deliberately picky about sub-commands: a compound command only auto-approves if *every* parsed segment matches a rule, and things like nested [INLINE_CODE] substitutions, added write redirects, or combos the tree-sitter parser can't decompose will still prompt.

Potential thoughts/plan forward:

- **Allow [INLINE_CODE] for this session**
- **Always allow exact command line [INLINE_CODE]** (persists to the [INLINE_CODE] setting)
- **Allow all commands in this session** — would want to align with the permissions / risk-assessment folks on how this interacts with the session permission model before wiring it up

Pointers for agent:

- AH: [INLINE_CODE], and [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE] path)
- Workbench reference for session-scoped rules: [INLINE_CODE] in [INLINE_CODE]

title: Support line range syntax in Quick Open (Go to File)
body:
### Feature request

In Quick Open (**Go to File**), you can type a file path followed by [INLINE_CODE] or [INLINE_CODE] to open a file at a specific position. It would be useful to also support a **line range** using a hyphen, so that pressing Enter opens the file with that range selected.

### Proposed syntax

- [INLINE_CODE] → select from the start of line 20 to the start of line 40
- [INLINE_CODE] → select from line 20, col 3 to line 40, col 5
- [INLINE_CODE] → end column defaults to the start of the end line
- Should also work with the existing separator/style variants: [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE]

This mirrors the range syntax VS Code already uses for markdown document links ([INLINE_CODE]), so a bare [INLINE_CODE] selects from the start of line 10 to the start of line 20.

### Notes

- The parsing lives in [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE]), which is reached through the file picker ([INLINE_CODE]).

Addressed by [#324318](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/324318).

(Written by Copilot)

title: Mouse back/forward buttons do not navigate in the Agents window
body:
The mouse back/forward buttons (buttons 4/5) navigate editor history in the main VS Code window, but do nothing in the Agents window.

This is inconsistent with the keyboard, where [INLINE_CODE] / [INLINE_CODE] already navigate between sessions in the Agents window.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Agents window.
2. Visit two or more sessions so there is session history.
3. Press the mouse back button.

**Expected:** navigate to the previously visited session, matching [INLINE_CODE].
**Actual:** nothing happens.

### Cause

The shared mouse handler in [INLINE_CODE] calls [INLINE_CODE] / [INLINE_CODE] on the **editor** history service directly, bypassing command and keybinding resolution. Since no [INLINE_CODE]-clause routing applies, the mouse never reaches the Agents window's session history ([INLINE_CODE], exposed through [INLINE_CODE] / [INLINE_CODE]), and the editor history it falls through to is usually empty in that window.

This is why the keyboard path works (it is routed by [INLINE_CODE] clauses on [INLINE_CODE]) while the mouse path does not.

### Notes

Both histories are intentionally live in the Agents window: editor history still applies to the docked side pane (Changes multi-diff, Files, file diffs). So the fix needs to route by focus rather than replace one with the other.

A possible broader follow-up is to have the [INLINE_CODE] mouse handler dispatch [INLINE_CODE] / [INLINE_CODE] through [INLINE_CODE] so [INLINE_CODE] clauses decide the target, which would give any window contributing higher-weight bindings for those chords mouse support automatically.

Fixed by #327432.

(Written by Copilot)

title: fix: enrich truncated IPC object deserialize error (fixes #330263)
body:
### Summary

Telemetry bucket [INLINE_CODE] reports [INLINE_CODE] thrown from [INLINE_CODE] inside [INLINE_CODE] in [INLINE_CODE], running in the agent host utility process ([INLINE_CODE]) while decoding an inbound IPC message delivered over a MessagePort. The message payload arrives truncated: the binary framing declares an object of N bytes, but fewer than N bytes are present, so [INLINE_CODE] on a partial/empty string fails with a context-free error that gives triage no way to see where the corruption happened. New in [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE]); not present in the [INLINE_CODE] baseline ([INLINE_CODE]), matching the introduction of the Agent Host Protocol-over-IPC (MessagePort) plumbing.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#330263
Recommended reviewer: [INLINE_CODE]

### Culprit Commit

Ancestry could not be git-verified in this environment (blobless checkout, credentials stripped after checkout, so [INLINE_CODE] / [INLINE_CODE] fail on on-demand object fetch). Within the [INLINE_CODE] to [INLINE_CODE] regression window, the agent-host MessagePort transport that routes these IPC messages was introduced/reworked by:

- [INLINE_CODE] — "agentHost: use AHP for local connections" (routes local renderer traffic through the Agent Host Protocol over MessagePort) — Connor Peet ([INLINE_CODE]).

This is the most likely producer of the new truncated-frame path; the crash surfaces in the shared [INLINE_CODE] utility rather than in the transport commit itself.

### Code Flow

[CODE_BLOCK]

### Affected Files

- [INLINE_CODE] — [INLINE_CODE] [INLINE_CODE] case (crash site and where the truncation first becomes observable). [INLINE_CODE] (lines 217-221) slices without erroring on underflow, so a short buffer silently yields a partial string.

### Repro Steps

Deterministic user repro is not available (the truncation originates in the native MessagePort/utility-process boundary during agent host connect/disconnect, not in reproducible TS logic). Observed across Windows/Mac/Linux, 44 users, on [INLINE_CODE]. Conceptually: deliver a MessagePort frame to the agent host whose binary object header declares more bytes than the payload actually contains (e.g. a partial/racing frame during agent host teardown) and [INLINE_CODE] will attempt [INLINE_CODE] on a truncated string.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE] [INLINE_CODE] case (the bypass site is [INLINE_CODE], where [INLINE_CODE] can return fewer than N bytes without error because [INLINE_CODE] slices without bounds-checking). Before calling [INLINE_CODE], read the declared length N and the actual buffer, and if the buffer is shorter than declared, throw an enriched error naming the expected vs. received byte counts. This follows the cross-process-error principle: enrich the error with diagnostic context, do not swallow it. The error is still thrown and still reaches the telemetry pipeline, but the new bucket will carry actionable framing information ([INLINE_CODE]) instead of an opaque [INLINE_CODE], letting the transport owner see truncation is occurring and where. This does not add a [INLINE_CODE], does not remove any [INLINE_CODE], and does not coerce the bad value to a benign default — the corrupt frame is still rejected loudly.

**Alternatives considered**
- Wrap [INLINE_CODE] in [INLINE_CODE] and return [INLINE_CODE]/empty object — rejected: swallows a real cross-process corruption, hides the producer, and breaks the telemetry signal that surfaced the bug.
- Drop empty/short messages at the producer in [INLINE_CODE] ([INLINE_CODE]) — rejected as the primary fix: the true producer is the native MessagePort layer (not visible in TS), the exact truncation condition isn't reconstructable from source, and silently dropping frames there would mask the corruption for every channel without diagnostics. Enriching at the deserialization boundary keeps the signal while making it diagnosable for whichever transport is at fault.

### Recommended Owner

[INLINE_CODE] — authored the 1.133 Agent Host Protocol-over-MessagePort IPC plumbing ([INLINE_CODE], "agentHost: use AHP for local connections") that introduced the new transport path in which this error appears.

title: agent host: assert minimum test counts in a validation script
body:
Follow-up from the scoped-enablement work (#330566, #330715).

## Problem

Three separate times during that work, a validation run **looked green while having verified nothing**:

1. **Stale [INLINE_CODE]** — the Electron unit runner exited [INLINE_CODE] having run no tests, because a merge left a stale compiled module and the runner died on an unrelated dynamic-import error. Fixed by [INLINE_CODE].
2. **Zero-match grep selector** — [INLINE_CODE] matched **no tests** and reported success-shaped output. The suites are capitalized ([INLINE_CODE]), and the real selector runs 35 tests. Three separate agents reported [INLINE_CODE] before anyone noticed the selector was wrong.
3. **Policy checks reading as build failures** — [INLINE_CODE] / [INLINE_CODE] reported [INLINE_CODE], but the check-run output title was [INLINE_CODE]: the build never ran. Easy to misread as a real regression and go hunting for a nonexistent bug.

In each case the tell was the same: a summary line that was empty or suspiciously small.

## Suggestion

A small [INLINE_CODE] (or npm script) that runs the standard agent-host validation set and **asserts a minimum test count** for each command, failing loudly when a run reports fewer tests than expected. That turns "suspiciously small summary" from something a human has to notice into a hard failure.

Current baselines on [INLINE_CODE] at time of writing:

[CODE_BLOCK]

- The unit runner uses pre-compiled output and does **not** fail on type errors — [INLINE_CODE] must be run separately.
- Electron runner setup aborts ([INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE]) are environmental; recover with [INLINE_CODE] rather than reading them as test failures.

title: Support auto model selection in .agent.md based on task complexity
body:
## Summary

Allow custom agents () to declare a **model selection policy** instead of (or in addition to) a static model, so VS Code can pick the best available model for each invocation based on task complexity, context size, or tool requirements.

## Problem

Currently, custom agents pin a single model (or a static fallback array) in frontmatter:

This creates a hard trade-off:

| Scenario | Static model choice | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Simple refactor ("add a type annotation") | Expensive / large model | Wastes tokens and money |
| Complex architecture analysis | Cheap / small model | Poor quality, misses nuance |
| High-tool-calling task (CI, k8s manifests) | Model without reliable tool calling | Fails silently or hallucinates tool args |
| Long-context summarization | Small-context model | Truncates, loses critical info |

Multi-agent setups amplify this: an orchestrator dispatches to 5+ phase agents, each hardcoded to one model. The orchestrator cannot adapt model selection to the workload it's handing off.

## Proposed solution

Add a (or ) frontmatter field alongside :

### How selection would work

1. VS Code already knows each model's capabilities from (tool calling, vision, max tokens, context window).
2. At invocation time, the agent framework inspects the user's request + tool set + conversation context length.
3. It selects the cheapest model whose capabilities satisfy the policy constraints.
4. If no model qualifies, fall back to the explicit list or the field.

### Capability-aware selection signals

| Signal | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Tool calling required | Agent's list is non-empty | Filter to models with |
| Large context | Conversation history + attachments > 64K tokens | Filter to models with ≥ context size |
| Vision needed | User attached image(s) | Filter to models with |
| Task complexity | User prompt heuristic (code analysis, multi-file refactor, architecture) | Prefer larger models when quality-first; smaller when cost-optimal |

### Interaction with existing field

model

## Why this matters

- **Cost**: Users with BYOK endpoints (token-plan models, self-hosted) pay per token. Routing trivial tasks to a 1M-context model is wasteful.
- **Quality**: Complex tasks on small models degrade the agent experience silently — the agent works but produces shallow output.
- **Orchestrator workflows**: Multi-agent setups (DE → SE → EM pattern, or CI pipeline agents) need per-task model selection. The orchestrator knows the phase but can't express it in the current model field.
- **Provider diversity**: As more BYOK providers are added (LM Studio, cloud endpoints, token plans), the selection problem grows combinatorially.

## Current workaround

Static fallback arrays with manual ordering:

This just picks the first available — it doesn't adapt to task needs.

## Related

- [#319709](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/319709) — Custom endpoint model resolution format (now resolved: format)
- capability fields (, , )
- Custom agent field documentation

title: Only show shimmer on non active chat tabs
body:
Currently:
When multiple chats are in progress within a session, there's an overload of progress indicators. 

Solution:
When a chat tab is in focus, that is also in progress, don't show progress indication at the tab level. Since that will already be taken care of by the in-progress response in the chat view.

title: Agent plugins: Install Plugin From Source deletes plugins installed from a marketplace on the same repository
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.138.0 (stable, commit 7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda). The code involved is unchanged on [INLINE_CODE] at 0dbdacd.
- OS Version: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)

When a marketplace is configured with a ref, running "Chat: Install Plugin From Source" on the same repository without a ref deletes the marketplace clone. Any plugin installed from that marketplace loses its files. The default value of [INLINE_CODE] includes [INLINE_CODE], so a default setup reproduces the problem.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. With default settings, open the Extensions view, search [INLINE_CODE], and install [INLINE_CODE] from [INLINE_CODE]. Accept the trust prompt.
2. Check that [INLINE_CODE] exists and that [INLINE_CODE] lists [INLINE_CODE].
3. Run "Chat: Install Plugin From Source", enter [INLINE_CODE], and accept the trust prompt.

[INLINE_CODE] is [INLINE_CODE]. I used a portable install, where the folder is [INLINE_CODE].

Result:

- The input box shows "No plugins found in 'github/awesome-copilot'. This does not appear to be a valid plugin marketplace." The [INLINE_CODE] branch of that repository has a [INLINE_CODE] that lists 162 plugins.
- The [INLINE_CODE] folder is deleted, including the [INLINE_CODE] clone.
- [INLINE_CODE] still lists [INLINE_CODE], and the plugin no longer loads.

Renderer log at trace level:

[CODE_BLOCK]

I reproduced this twice, the second time from an empty portable profile. Running step 3 again right after the failure works: VS Code clones [INLINE_CODE] and lists the plugins. Only the failing run started with the [INLINE_CODE] clone on disk.

Expected: the source install clones the repository and leaves the marketplace clone in place. A failed install removes only the files that install created.

Likely cause, from reading the source on [INLINE_CODE]:

The marketplace clone for [INLINE_CODE] goes in [INLINE_CODE]. [INLINE_CODE] builds its source descriptor without a ref, so [INLINE_CODE] returns the parent folder, [INLINE_CODE]. Because that folder already exists, [INLINE_CODE] skips the clone. The folder root has no manifest, so [INLINE_CODE] calls [INLINE_CODE], which deletes the folder recursively.

The shared-cache check in [INLINE_CODE] does not run on this path, because the call passes no [INLINE_CODE]. The check also compares paths for equality, so it would not detect a clone nested below the target. [INLINE_CODE] uses the same folder layout, so a git URL marketplace with a ref, such as an Azure DevOps remote, has the same problem.

Separately, [INLINE_CODE] parses a [INLINE_CODE] in the input but drops the ref from the source descriptor, so a source install always clones the default branch.

Some ways to fix the collision:

- Give ref-less source clones a folder that cannot contain a [INLINE_CODE] folder, such as a [INLINE_CODE] segment.
- Check that an existing folder is a git work tree before skipping the clone.
- On failure, delete the folder only when the current install created it.

title: Agent Host: permission mode can race managed-settings resolution
body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Problem

A Copilot Agent Host session can attempt to apply the VS Code-configured [INLINE_CODE] permission mode before the SDK/runtime has finished resolving managed settings. The runtime then rejects the mode and the turn fails with:

[CODE_BLOCK]

This appears intermittently and is most visible when managed settings disable bypass permissions or resolution temporarily enters a fail-closed state.

## Current behavior

- [INLINE_CODE] derives [INLINE_CODE] from root/session configuration.
- [INLINE_CODE] sends that value through [INLINE_CODE] at turn start.
- Managed settings are resolved independently by the runtime. The [INLINE_CODE] event is currently projected into session sandbox policy, but not into effective approval/permission state.
- [INLINE_CODE] logs and continues when the managed-settings event has not arrived before post-launch sandbox configuration.

The resulting state can briefly advertise or select Allow All while the runtime has already disallowed bypass, causing the SDK RPC to reject rather than clamping the effective mode before the turn starts.

## Expected behavior

Session startup and turn preparation should have an authoritative managed-permission boundary. VS Code should not request [INLINE_CODE] until managed settings are resolved and permit bypass. A restrictive or fail-closed result should update the effective permission mode and picker state before sending the turn.

## Related

- #335928 tracks picker/runtime behavior for [INLINE_CODE].
- #330036 was a separate managed-settings schema failure involving [INLINE_CODE].
- #330349 handled legacy-setting transport ordering; it does not establish a runtime managed-settings readiness barrier for permission mode.
